extensions: Derive the top-ten list from click-event analytics ranked by 30-day frequency per user cohort, not product intuition — instrument each dashboard action with a named event and rank by frequency. This makes the shortcut set defensible and adjustable as usage patterns shift without re-shipping code.

Add a conflict detection layer at registration time: before binding any shortcut, check it against browser-reserved keys and OS shortcuts. Surface conflicts to the developer at build time via a linting step rather than discovering them at runtime.

Expose shortcuts as a user-configurable key map stored in the user's profile record (JSON column or dedicated key_bindings table), requiring a settings UI panel, server-side persistence layer, and client-side binding resolver that reads the user's stored map on session initialisation.

Implement a shortcut hint overlay triggered by holding a modifier key (e.g. Alt) that overlays badge labels on each actionable element showing its bound key — contextual in-place discovery rather than a static modal.
nonObviousAngles: This feature is a natural forcing function for building a command registry — a central map of { actionId -> { handler, label, shortcut } } that the entire app routes through. Done right, the shortcut system becomes the action bus that future automation features (command palette, voice control, macro recording) extend for free.

Keyboard shortcut sets are a localisation and accessibility surface that most teams discover late. Keys convenient on a US QWERTY layout may conflict with IME bindings on Japanese or Korean keyboards, or with platform-level shortcuts on macOS vs Windows. If the user base is international, the default key map needs review against at least three keyboard layouts before ship.

weaknesses.text: The assumption that the dashboard contains no rich text editors or input components that swallow global keydown events is unverified. A global keydown listener will fire inside input fields unless every handler explicitly checks event.target. A shortcut triggering a destructive action while the user is typing is a data-corruption or accidental-submission risk that is invisible in testing but catastrophic in production.
weaknesses.label: blocking

weaknesses.text: User-configurable key bindings stored server-side and resolved client-side on session init create a race condition: if the fetch is not complete when the first shortcut fires, the binding resolver returns undefined with no defined degradation spec. This produces inconsistent behaviour that is nearly impossible to reproduce in local dev where the fetch completes in <10ms.
weaknesses.label: blocking

weaknesses.text: The conflict-detection extension claims build-time detection of browser extension conflicts. Browser extension conflicts cannot be detected at build time — they are runtime environment variables that differ per user machine. Claiming this creates false confidence in the conflict-detection system.
weaknesses.label: blocking

weaknesses.text: The analytics-derived top-ten list is per user cohort, not per user. A power-user cohort likely includes users with very different action distributions. The cohort-average top ten may be low-value for the individual user's actual workflow, undermining the stated goal.
weaknesses.label: resolvable

weaknesses.text: The Alt-held hint overlay fires a DOM traversal to find actionable elements and append badge nodes on every keydown. On a dashboard with 50–100 interactive elements, holding Alt during dashboard activity will cause perceptible jank on low-end hardware because badge insertion forces layout recalculation.
weaknesses.label: resolvable

risks: If the top-ten action list is hardcoded at ship time and analytics prove it is wrong, updating requires a code change and deploy — users who have memorised shortcuts will experience a breaking change with no migration path.

Screen reader and assistive technology users have a legal expectation (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4) that single-key shortcuts can be turned off or require a modifier. If shortcuts ship as modifier-free keys, the feature is non-compliant by default.
The key_bindings table being on the same database as application data means a failed schema migration during rollback drops user-saved preferences with no recovery path.
failureModes: A power user's profile fetch fails silently due to a transient database timeout. The client falls back to defaults (if that path is even implemented). They spend 20 minutes wondering why their shortcuts reset. Support cannot reproduce the failure because it leaves no trace if the fetch error is swallowed.

The shortcut 'Submit Application' is bound to Ctrl+Enter. A mortgage advisor presses Ctrl+Enter in a textarea to add a line break. The input-focus guard has a bug on a specific browser version. The application submits with an incomplete note, irreversibly.

Analytics identifies 'Export to PDF' as a top-ten action because users click it repeatedly due to slow response times. The shortcut makes it trivially easy to queue 10 export jobs in two seconds, degrading server performance for all users during end-of-month peaks.

userChallenges: The top-ten list by 30-day frequency per cohort shortcuts actions that users click most often — but high-click-frequency actions are often high-frequency precisely because they are slow or buried in the UI. Shortcutting the symptom (repeated clicking) rather than fixing the navigation problem may deliver zero felt improvement.

The Alt-held hint overlay requires users to already know the overlay exists before they can discover shortcuts. The feature that teaches you shortcuts is itself hidden behind a shortcut — a known discoverability failure pattern.

User-configurable key maps create a cross-device consistency expectation the application may not honour uniformly. When the key map silently fails to load, the user presses a key expecting one action and triggers a different one, with no visible indication that their personal map failed to resolve.

The conflict detection extension covers browser-reserved keys at registration time — a single snapshot. Browser extensions are added and removed continuously. A binding that passes detection today may collide with a newly installed extension next month, and the user has no feedback mechanism to diagnose which layer intercepted the keypress.
adoptionRisks: Power users who already have a workflow worth optimising almost certainly have an existing workaround — browser macros, OS-level key remapping, or a muscle-memory click sequence. Unless the application's shortcuts are immediately available in every context where the workaround currently works, the workaround wins.

The settings UI required for user-configurable key maps is adoption friction at exactly the wrong moment. Fewer than 15% of users who encounter a customisation surface complete a configuration change. The majority revert to defaults or abandon the feature.

The feature targets the ten most frequently used actions by cohort median — but the users most likely to adopt shortcuts are outlier power users whose own top-ten may differ significantly from the median. If a power user's most-used action is not in the shortcut set, the feature delivers no value to its stated target.

When a shortcut silently fails — focus state, extension conflict, key map load failure — the user receives no feedback. A single silent failure during the first week of adoption is sufficient to cause permanent reversion to prior behaviour.

strengths: The command registry pattern (ShortcutManager singleton) is architecturally correct — it makes the system composable and extensible to command-palette and macro-recording use cases without a rewrite.
Analytics-derived shortcut selection is the right measurement strategy — it lets actual usage data drive the next iteration rather than product intuition.
The Alt-held contextual badge overlay is a better discoverability pattern than a static modal — surfacing shortcuts at the point of action is what drives adoption.
suggestedPivots: Implement the input-focus guard as the very first engineering task — before any binding is written. It is safety-critical code that must be correct before any shortcut can ship.

Define the key-map degradation contract explicitly before building: fall back to default bindings until user profile resolves, then hot-swap. This must be a spec decision, not an implementation afterthought.
openQuestions: Does the dashboard contain rich text editors, contenteditable elements, or third-party input components that would swallow global shortcut bindings when focused?
Does the codebase have action-level analytics events at sufficient granularity to produce a data-driven top-ten list, or will this require a discovery step first?
Is the dashboard SPA using route-level component teardown that would cause a root listener to re-register on navigation?
